newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee consumption stagnant in 1996 - DKV.
newsitem.headline: German coffee consumption stagnant in 1996 - DKV.

text.p: German coffee sales in 1996 retain the steady patterns noted in the first six months, Frieder Rotzolll, the managing director of the German coffee industry association (DKV) said on Wednesday.
"It is a stagnant market despite a colder than average summer," he said during an espresso promotion event.
Green coffee equivalent sales of roasted and soluble coffee in 1995 were 564,000 tonnes, down 2.5 percent from 1994.
Rotzoll said the only two areas bucking the trend were flavoured instant coffees and espresso.
Instant coffees have a steady 10 percent share of the German market, the world's second largest after the U.S., while espresso last acocunted for 1.5 percent.

Espresso was becoming increasingly popular in sales outside the home such as restaurants and canteens, where consumers favoured its southern European appeal associated with travel and sunshine, DKV said.
Jura GmbH, a Swiss vendor of espresso machines which organised the press conference, also saw growth opportunities in sales to private households.
